purpose: Teach: 閉会/ゲン/ヘルス/賜り/設問/緊密/同点/勧める

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 蓮、学会の閉会、印象に残る発表、目指して、頑張れ、本当に、若いうちに、経験、積めよ、絶対、君の財産になるからな、絶対、頼んだぞ、本気で、本当に、頑張れ。
lines.en: Ren — nail that conference presentation. Make it memorable. You're young; this is the time to build that kind of experience. It'll become your real asset. I mean it. Give it everything you've got.
lines.style: Steady, deliberate opening. Measured warmth beneath the direction. Emphasizes key phrases with quiet weight — not lecturing, guiding. Slight lean forward in the voice. Ends firm but not cold.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。研究者でも、ゲン担ぎ、する人、いらっしゃるそうですね、本当に、興味深いです、私も、最近、密かに、しております、本当に、効くんですよ、結構、本当に、絶対。
lines.en: Yes. You know, even researchers do things for luck — I've heard that. It's actually fascinating. I've been doing a little of it myself lately, to be honest. And it really does work. Truly.
lines.style: Earnest, a touch embarrassed to admit the superstition. Picks up tempo slightly when defending the idea — genuine conviction. Soft trailing-off on final affirmation, like he's still discovering it's okay to believe in this.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 研究者として、健康、ヘルスケア、本気で、考えろ、長く、研究、続けるためにも、絶対、自分の体、大事にしろ、絶対に、本気だぞ、本当に、頼んだ、絶対、本気で。
lines.en: But as a researcher, take your health seriously. Really seriously. You need to stay well to keep researching for the long haul. Your body matters. Take care of it. I'm not being casual about this.
lines.style: Shifts to firm, almost parental tone. Deliberate pace. Each phrase lands. Not angry — genuine concern underneath the directness. The voice of someone who has seen people burn out.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。先生から、ご指導、本当に、賜り、感謝、申し上げております、社会人になっても、絶対、活かしてまいります、本当に、ありがたいです、いつも、本気、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. I'm truly grateful for everything you've taught me, sir. I'll carry it forward when I enter the workforce, absolutely. And thank you for always being there when I need guidance. I mean that sincerely.
lines.style: Respectful, careful articulation. Warmth beneath the formality — not stiff, but honoring the relationship. Slight hesitation before key gratitudes, as if making sure each one lands with sincerity.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 論文の設問、独自の視点で、立てろ、独創性、評価されるからな、絶対、君も、視野、広げて、独自性、出していけ、本当に、頼んだぞ、絶対、本気で、本当に。
lines.en: Your thesis questions — frame them from your own perspective. That's what gets noticed: originality. Expand your thinking. Develop your own voice in this work. Really commit to it. I'm counting on you.
lines.style: Direct, almost commanding but not unkind. Crisp opening on each new instruction. Voice settles lower on key words — 'originality,' 'your own voice.' Ends with quiet emphasis that carries weight.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。指導教官と、緊密に、連絡を、取り合うようにしております、本当に、感謝、しております、いつでも、相談、乗ってくださって、本気で、絶対、ありがたいです、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. I'm staying in close contact with my adviser, actually. I'm really grateful for that — he makes himself available whenever I need to talk something through. It means a lot to me.
lines.style: Thoughtful, appreciative tone. Speaks clearly about the support without overselling it. Quiet pride in having found that resource. Genuine warmth when mentioning the adviser's availability.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 同期と、研究で、同点の競争、続けることも、君の刺激になるぞ、絶対、頑張れ、本当に、楽しみだぞ、君の、これから、本気で、応援してるからな、絶対、本当に。
lines.en: Working alongside your cohort — that kind of friendly competition will push you forward. It's good for you. Keep at it. I'm honestly looking forward to seeing where you take this. I'm rooting for you. Really.
lines.style: Warm encouragement with genuine interest. Picks up energy when discussing the peer dynamic. Final phrase settles into quiet sincerity — not performative, but real. Voice softens slightly on 'really.'

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。先生に、最新の論文、ご紹介させて、いただきたいです、本当に、勧めるに値する、内容だと、思っております、本気で、絶対、お読み、頂きたいです、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. I'd like to share the latest paper with you, if I may. I think it's genuinely worth your time — the research is solid. I really do hope you'll read it.
lines.style: Respectful but genuine enthusiasm. Slight hesitation before offering — seeking permission even though it's collaborative. Picks up tempo slightly when describing the paper's quality. Ends with understated conviction.
